domain_symbols.analytic_object: continuous, discrete, and variational analytic objects

rules.name: Gamma recurrence seed
rules.input_form: gamma-function argument in the standard domain
preconditions: The gamma function is evaluated away from its singular set
rules.operation: Extend factorial structure by the gamma recurrence relation.
examples: Factorial identities extend from integers to broader arguments through gamma recurrence
counterexamples: Treating gamma as a polynomial extension of factorial is invalid

rules.name: Bessel-type differential seed
rules.input_form: canonical differential operator with singular or symmetry-adapted structure
preconditions: A canonical operator equation is fixed
rules.operation: Define a special-function family through a characteristic operator equation.
examples: Bessel families arise from radial-separation problems and are governed by a characteristic second-order equation
counterexamples: Arbitrary functions with no defining operator relation are not special-function families in this sense

rules.name: Linear difference equation seed
rules.input_form: discrete recurrence relation with linear structure
preconditions: A discrete index set and linear recurrence are fixed
rules.operation: Model discrete evolution by a linear recurrence relation.
examples: Recursively defined sequences can be solved by characteristic or variation-style discrete methods when linear structure is present
counterexamples: Replacing shift relations by unrelated pointwise formulas destroys the recurrence model

rules.name: Weierstrass approximation seed
rules.input_form: continuous function on a compact interval
preconditions: The function is continuous on a compact interval
rules.operation: Approximate continuous functions uniformly by polynomials.
examples: Polynomial families provide dense approximants to continuous targets on closed bounded intervals
counterexamples: Expecting exact finite-degree representation for every continuous function is invalid

rules.name: Best approximation seed
rules.input_form: target object, approximation class, and error norm
rules.output_form: optimal approximant relative to the chosen geometry
preconditions: An approximation class and metric or norm are fixed
rules.operation: Minimize approximation error relative to the active norm or metric.
examples: Least-squares and uniform approximation problems depend on the error geometry selected in advance
counterexamples: Claiming one approximation is universally best without specifying the error metric is invalid

rules.name: Euler-Lagrange seed
rules.input_form: smooth functional on an admissible family
preconditions: An admissible variational class and smooth integrand are fixed
rules.operation: Pass from stationary functional behavior to Euler-Lagrange equations.
examples: Minimizing an action functional leads to differential equations for admissible paths or fields
counterexamples: Optimizing over arbitrary discontinuous competitors without admissibility structure is invalid

rules.name: Elliptic index bridge seed
rules.input_form: elliptic operator on a global geometric object
preconditions: An elliptic operator and global manifold-type setting are fixed
rules.operation: Relate analytic index data of an elliptic operator to global topological invariants.
examples: Local differential operators can encode global topological information through index constructions
counterexamples: Treating purely local operator coefficients as the whole story of global index behavior is invalid

rules.name: Hypergeometric equation seed
rules.input_form: parameterized second-order hypergeometric-type differential equation
preconditions: A hypergeometric-type differential equation and parameter regime are fixed
rules.operation: Organize special functions through hypergeometric differential-equation structure.
examples: Classical orthogonal and special functions can often be organized as specializations of hypergeometric structure
counterexamples: Arbitrary parameterized functions with no governing differential equation are not automatically hypergeometric families

rules.name: Nonlinear recurrence fixed-point seed
rules.input_form: nonlinear update map with parameterized iteration
preconditions: A nonlinear recurrence map and iteration domain are fixed
rules.operation: Study nonlinear discrete evolution through fixed points, stability, and parameter-driven regime changes.
examples: Discrete iteration can exhibit stable, unstable, or oscillatory regimes even when the update rule is elementary
counterexamples: Assuming every nonlinear recurrence behaves like a linear recurrence is invalid

rules.name: Chebyshev minimax seed
rules.input_form: uniform approximation problem on a compact domain
preconditions: A compact domain and finite-dimensional approximation family are fixed
rules.operation: Characterize best uniform approximation through minimax structure and alternation behavior.
examples: Best uniform approximants are controlled by extremal error patterns rather than only average error size
counterexamples: Minimizing pointwise error at one location does not by itself produce a minimax-optimal approximant

rules.name: Noether symmetry seed
rules.input_form: action functional with continuous symmetry
preconditions: A smooth variational problem and symmetry action are fixed
rules.operation: Generate conserved quantities from continuous variational symmetries.
examples: Time-translation invariance leads to an energy-type conservation law in many classical action models
counterexamples: Arbitrary transformations with no variational symmetry do not automatically generate conserved quantities

rules.name: Heat kernel asymptotic seed
rules.input_form: elliptic or Laplace-type operator on a geometric object
preconditions: A heat-type operator and global geometric setting are fixed
rules.operation: Relate short-time heat-kernel behavior to geometric and spectral structure.
examples: Local curvature or operator data can influence short-time diffusion signatures in a global geometric model
counterexamples: Treating heat propagation as independent of the operator or geometry is invalid

rules.name: Canonical form normalization expansion
rules.input_form: raw expression E
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Rewrite expressions into a canonical form that preserves the active equivalence relation.
examples: x + y and y + x map to a shared canonical additive form in commutative settings
counterexamples: Applying canonicalization rules outside their preconditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Substitution soundness expansion
rules.input_form: expression F(x) with admissible substitution x <- g
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Substitute only under explicit domain and structural admissibility constraints.
examples: Replacing a variable by a constrained expression must preserve declared domain assumptions
counterexamples: Substitution that violates assumptions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Composition rule expansion

rules.name: Solver branch admissibility expansion

rules.name: Degenerate case handling expansion
